title: Resonantly Enhanced Multiphonon Scattering and Local Orbital-Phonon Coupling in Bulk and Thin Flakes of 2D Single Crystals of Antiferromagnetic (NixFe1-x)2P2S6
authors: Nasaru Khan, Miłosz Rybak, Yuliia Shemerliuk, Sebastian Selter, Bernd Büchner, Saicharan Aswartham, Krzysztof Wohlfeld, Pradeep Kumar
abstract: Orbital degrees of freedom play a pivotal role in shaping the physical properties of two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals magnetic systems, strongly influencing electron-phonon coupling and intermediate-state dynamics. In this study, we present a comprehensive temperature and thickness-dependent Raman investigation of the single crystals of 2D van der Waals antiferromagnetic series (NixFe1-x)2P2S6. Utilizing Raman spectroscopy, we explore the interplay between local orbital excitations and lattice vibrations, observing higher-order phonon modes extending up to the fourth order. We observe an anomalously high and weakly temperature-dependent intensity ratio of these higher-order modes relative to low-energy first-order phonons. Theoretical cluster calculations and Franck-Condon modelling reveal that these features originate from resonantly enhanced multiphonon scattering mediated by localized intermediate Ni 3d8 multiplet excitations. The local orbital occupancy of these intermediate states couples strongly to lattice coordinates, providing a selective enhancement mechanism for specific phonon channels. Notably, these higher-order features are absent in the end-member Fe2P2S6. This distinction reflects the charge-transfer character of Ni2P2S6, which places optical transitions in resonance with local multiplet states, contrasted with the Mott-Hubbard insulator regime in Fe-rich analogues. Our findings clarify the microscopic origin of high-frequency Raman scattering in transition metal thiophosphates and underscore the central role of local orbital-phonon interactions in 2D correlated magnets.
summary: This work uses Raman spectroscopy to study 2D antiferromagnetic materials, finding that high-frequency scattering is not due to simple phonon overtones. Instead, the intensity is resonantly enhanced by localized Ni 3d electronic excitations, confirming the crucial role of local orbital-phonon coupling in these correlated magnets.
main_problem: To determine the microscopic origin of anomalously strong, high-frequency Raman scattering in 2D van der Waals antiferromagnetic materials, focusing on the interplay between local orbital excitations and lattice vibrations.
main_result: The high-frequency scattering is attributed to resonantly enhanced multiphonon scattering mediated by localized Ni 3d8 multiplet excitations, which is distinct from standard phonon overtones.
method: Temperature and thickness-dependent Raman spectroscopy, complemented by theoretical cluster calculations and Franck-Condon modeling.
model_or_system: The study investigates 2D single crystals of antiferromagnetic (Ni_xFe_{1-x})2P2S6, comparing the charge-transfer character of Ni2P2S6 with the Mott-Hubbard insulator regime of Fe2P2S6.
key_observables: Anomalously high and weakly temperature-dependent intensity ratio of higher-order modes relative to low-energy first-order phonons; specific phonon clusters around 800 cm-1 and 1170 cm-1.
important_parameters: Temperature (4 K to 300 K); crystal thickness (down to 10 nm); doping concentration (x in Ni_xFe_{1-x}).
main_assumptions: The anomalous scattering behavior suggests resonance phenomena involving localized Ni 3d8 multiplets, rather than simple harmonic overtones.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate raw and fitted Raman spectra for varying flake thicknesses, showing specific peak clusters; temperature dependence plots track mode softening and anomalies near the AFM transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes Raman spectra across varying thicknesses and compositions, contrasting the observed high-order features in Ni-containing compounds against the background of established phonon modes and theoretical expectations.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between electronic excitations (Ni 3d orbitals) and lattice vibrations (phonons) provides a concrete, measurable example of strong electron-phonon coupling in a correlated magnetic system, relevant to understanding charge transfer and orbital ordering.
